'''Cynthia Zang Facer Clark''' {{post-nominals|country=UK|FRSS}} (born April 1, 1942){{r|born}} is an American statistician known for her work improving the quality of data in the [[federal statistical system]], and especially in the [[National Agricultural Statistics Service]].{{r|isua|nasda}} She has also served as the president of the [[Caucus for Women in Statistics]]{{r|cws}} and the Washington Statistical Society.{{r|isicws}} {{as of|2018}} she is executive director of the Council of Professional Associations on Federal Statistics.{{r|aera}}

==Early life and education==
Clark was born on April 1, 1942, the daughter of banker Joseph Elmer Facer and his wife Flora Burnell Zang Facer. She grew up in [[Colorado]],{{r|born|nass}} and was part of the class of 1960 at [[East High School (Denver)|East High School]] in [[Denver]].{{r|ehs}} She graduated in 1963 from [[Mills College]],{{r|mills}} where she majored in mathematics, and in the same year married Glenn Willett Clark, with whom she had six children.{{r|born|nass}}
She earned a master's degree from the [[University of Denver]] in 1964.{{r|aera|denver}}

She came to [[Iowa State University]] planning to continue in pure mathematics,{{r|adventure}} but completed her Ph.D. there in 1977 in statistics. Her dissertation was titled ''Convergence and ergodicity for conditional distributions: theory and applications'', and was supervised by Herbert T. David.{{r|diss}}

==Career==
In the late 1970s and early 1980s, Clark worked at the Office of Federal Statistical Policy and its successor agency, the [[Office of Management and Budget]].{{r|isua|cu}} She joined the [[National Agricultural Statistics Service]] in 1990, and created the [[Agricultural Resource Management Survey]] there. She was associate director for methodology and standards at the [[United States Census Bureau]] from 1996 to 2004.{{r|isua|cu}}

After three years in England as executive director for methodology and quality in the [[Office for National Statistics]] from 2004 to 2007, she returned to the National Agricultural Statistics Service in 2008 as its administrator.{{r|aera|cnstat}} After six years as administrator, she retired from federal service in 2014.{{r|nasda|cnstat}}

Since December 2018 she has been the executive director of the Council of Professional Associations on Federal Statistics.{{r|aera}}

==Service==
Clark served as president of the [[Caucus for Women in Statistics]] in 1989,{{r|cws}} and chaired the Committee on Women in Statistics of the [[International Statistical Institute]] from 2003 until 2011.{{r|isicws}}  She has also chaired the Government Statistics Section of the [[American Statistical Association]],{{r|aera}} and was president of the Washington Statistical Society for the 2000–2001 term.{{r|isicws}}

On her retirement, Clark and her husband served a mission to the [[Nauvoo Illinois Temple]] of [[the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]].{{r|cnstat}}

==Recognition==
In 1997, Clark was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fasa}} She is also an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]],{{r|isi}} and a fellow of the [[Royal Statistical Society]].{{r|aera}}

Clark was given a [[Presidential Rank Awards|Presidential Meritorious Rank Award]] in 2011.{{r|aera}}
The Iowa State University Alumni Association gave her their Distinguished Alumni Award in 2014.{{r|isua|adventure}}
